nodes.summary: For an element $y$ and lists $zs$ and $l$, if the list $y$ followed by $zs$ is a subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) of $l$, then there is a list $s$ such that $y$ followed by $s$ is a suffix of $l$ and $zs$ is a subsequence of $s$.
nodes.title: A subsequence starting with $y$ starts at an occurrence of $y$

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be an element, $rest$ a list, and $t$ a table of triples $(y, k, zs)$ that satisfies the invariant of the LIS table for $rest$. Let $(b, w)$ be the result of the scan of $t$ for entries above $x$. Then $(b + 1, w)$ is a table cell for $x$ followed by $rest$: $w$ is a subsequence of $rest$, the list $x$ followed by $w$ is strictly increasing and has length $b + 1$, and every strictly increasing list $x$…
nodes.title: The step of the LIS recurrence

nodes.summary: For an element $x$, lists $s$ and $zs$, and a natural number $k$, the pair $(k, zs)$ is a table cell for $x$ followed by $s$ when $zs$ is a subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) of $s$, the list $x$ followed by $zs$ is strictly increasing (each element strictly less than every later one) and has length $k$, and for every subsequence $zs'$ of $s$ such that $x$ followed by $zs'$ is strictly increasing, the list…
nodes.title: Table cell of the LIS dynamic program

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a preorder, the length of the list returned by the quadratic longest-increasing-subsequence program on $xs$ is the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$.
nodes.title: The quadratic LIS program attains the optimal length

nodes.summary: For a list $xs$ over a preorder and a natural number $k$, $k$ is the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$ when some strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$ has length $k$ and every strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$ has length at most $k$. Here a subsequence need not be contiguous, and strictly increasing means that each element is strictly less than every later one.
nodes.title: Length of a longest increasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a preorder and every natural number $k$, the list returned by the quadratic longest-increasing-subsequence program on $xs$ has length $k$ if and only if $k$ is the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the quadratic LIS program, by length

nodes.summary: The table of a list is a list of triples $(y, k, zs)$, built from the right: the empty list has the empty table, and the table of $x$ followed by $rest$ is the table $t$ of $rest$ with the entry $(x, b + 1, w)$ put in front, where $(b, w)$ is the result of the scan of $t$ for entries above $x$. Building the table costs the total cost of these scans.
nodes.title: Table of the quadratic LIS program

nodes.summary: A table $t$ of triples $(y, k, zs)$ satisfies the invariant for a list $l$ when every entry $(y, k, zs)$ of $t$ has a list $s$ such that $y$ followed by $s$ is a suffix of $l$ and $(k, zs)$ is a table cell for $y$ followed by $s$, and conversely, for every element $y$ and list $s$ such that $y$ followed by $s$ is a suffix of $l$, some entry $(y, k, zs)$ of $t$ makes $(k, zs)$ a table cell for $y$ followed by $s$.
nodes.title: Invariant of the LIS table

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a preorder, the list returned by the quadratic longest-increasing-subsequence program on $xs$ is a subsequence of $xs$, is strictly increasing (each element strictly less than every later one), and is at least as long as every strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the quadratic LIS program

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of length $n$ over a preorder, twice the cost of the quadratic longest-increasing-subsequence program on $xs$ equals $n(n + 1)$, so the program costs exactly $n(n + 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Running time of the quadratic LIS program

nodes.summary: Given a list $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ of elements of a preorder with decidable $<$, this timed computation builds, from the right, a table recording for each position $i$ a length and a strictly increasing subsequence starting with $x_i$ (the longest one, by the recurrence $L_i = 1 + \max \{ L_j : i < j,\ x_i < x_j \}$ with $\max \emptyset = 0$), and returns the stored subsequence of an entry of largest length, or the…
nodes.title: Longest increasing subsequence by dynamic programming

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a preorder with decidable $<$. For every value $x \in \alpha$ and every list $t$ of entries $(y, k, zs)$, where $y \in \alpha$, $k$ is a natural number and $zs$ is a list over $\alpha$, the scan of $t$ for the best table entry above $x$ costs exactly the length of $t$.
nodes.title: Cost of the scan for the best entry above a value

nodes.summary: Given a value $x$ and a list $t$ of entries $(y, k, zs)$, where $y$ is a value, $k$ a natural number and $zs$ a list of values, this timed computation returns the pair of $k$ and the list $y$ followed by $zs$ for an entry of $t$ with $x < y$ whose $k$ is largest among such entries, provided that $k$ is positive; if no entry with $x < y$ has $k > 0$, it returns $0$ and the empty list. It costs one unit per entry of…
nodes.title: Best table entry above a value

nodes.summary: Given a list $t$ of entries $(y, k, zs)$, where $k$ is a natural number and $zs$ is a list with elements of the same type as $y$, this timed computation returns the pair of $k$ and the list $y$ followed by $zs$ for an entry of $t$ whose $k$ is largest, provided that this $k$ is positive, and returns $0$ and the empty list otherwise (in particular when $t$ is empty). It costs one unit per entry of $t$.
nodes.title: Table entry of largest length

nodes.summary: For lists $P$ and $t = (t_0, \dots, t_{m-1})$ over a linear order, the invariant holds for the processed prefix $P$ and the tails $t$ when three conditions hold: $t$ is strictly increasing; for every $k < m$ some strictly increasing subsequence of $P$ of length $k + 1$ has last element $t_k$; and every nonempty strictly increasing subsequence of $P$, of length $\ell$ and with last element $y$, satisfies…
nodes.title: Patience sorting invariant

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, the value returned by patience sorting on $xs$ equals the length of the list returned on $xs$ by the quadratic dynamic program for a longest strictly increasing subsequence.
nodes.title: Patience sorting agrees with the quadratic dynamic program

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, the value returned by patience sorting on $xs$ is the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$: some strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$ has this length, and no strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$ is longer.
nodes.title: Correctness of patience sorting

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of length $n$ over a linear order, patience sorting on $xs$ uses at most $n \lceil \log_2 (n + 1) \rceil$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for patience sorting

nodes.summary: Given a list $xs$ over a linear order, patience sorting runs the patience scan of $xs$ starting from the empty array of tails and returns the size of the resulting array. Its cost is the number of comparisons made by the scan.
nodes.title: Patience sorting

nodes.summary: Given an array of tails and a list over a linear order, the patience scan applies the patience step to the elements of the list in order: on the empty list it returns the tails unchanged, and on a list $x$ followed by $xs$ it applies the patience step for $x$ to the tails and then runs the patience scan of $xs$ from the result. Its cost is the total cost of the steps.
nodes.title: Patience scan

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. For every array $t$ over $\alpha$ and every element $x \in \alpha$, the array returned by the patience step for $x$ on $t$ has size at most the size of $t$ plus $1$.
nodes.title: A patience step grows the tails by at most one

nodes.summary: Given an array $t$ of tails and an element $x$ over a linear order, let $i$ be the index returned by the lower-bound binary search for $x$ in $t$. If $i$ is less than the size of $t$, the step replaces the entry of $t$ at index $i$ by $x$; otherwise it appends $x$ to $t$. Its cost is the number of comparisons made by the binary search.
nodes.title: Patience step

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list and $t$ an array of tails over a linear order such that the patience sorting invariant holds for $P$ and the entries of $t$. Then for every list $xs$, the invariant holds for $P$ followed by $xs$ and the entries of the array returned by the patience scan of $xs$ from $t$.
nodes.title: The patience scan preserves the invariant

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of elements of a preorder and all natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, if both $k$ and $k'$ are the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of $xs$, then $k = k'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the longest increasing subsequence length

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
